{{stat|Health}} is the amount of damage a unit can survive before being downed.

=== Post-Combat Health Regen ===
{{#section-h:Constitution|Post-Combat Health Regen}}

=== Health Regen ===
{{stat|Health Regen}} is the amount of {{stat|health}} a unit heals at the end of each of their turns.

This healing counts as the unit healing themselves and will be boosted by any effects that increase the amount of healing that unit has.

Units do not have innate health regen and largely comes from the {{st|Health Regen}} status effect, but has some other sources:
<details>
<summary>Other sources of Health Regen</summary>
* {{st|Health Regen (Diminishing)}}
* {{p|Good Vibrations}}
* {{p|Thrill of the Hunt|+}}
* {{set|Medical}}
* {{tile|Flower}}
* {{tile|Tall Flower}}
* {{we|Blessed Day}}
</details>

=== Notes ===
* {{stat|Shield}} will be damaged before {{stat|Health}}.
* {{stat|Holy Shield}} will be damaged before {{stat|Shield}}.
** Certain damage sources ignore both types of Shield.
** A normal unit will die when running out of Health, regardless if they have Shield.

* Certain units have set 0 max health, surviving only with {{stat|Shield}}.
** Any attack that ignores Shield will kill them immedietdly.

* {{en|Übercat}} has uncapped health.

== Downed ==
When a unit runs out of {{stat|health}}, they are downed.

Downed units do not take turns.

A downed unit's body will use {{stat|Corpse Health}}.

Being downed removes the vast majority of status effects from that unit.

Most passive and item effects are disabled while downed.

=== Corpse Health ===
{{stat|Corpse Health}} is the amount of hits a unit's corpse can survive before being destroyed permanently.


Each damaging attack reduces Corpse Health by 1, regardless of amount of damage.
* If a corpse takes damage with knockback, it colliding into something will not damage it again. 
** Having something collide into it will still damage it however.

Units who have more than 1 Corpse Health can have their Corpse Health increased by healing their corpse.
* Each instance of {{icon|Heal|healing}} or added {{icon|Shield}} or {{icon|Holy Shield}} increases their Corpse Health by 1, regardless of amount of healing.


Player Cats have a base value of 3, while enemies can range from 0 to 5.
* Cats can have it affected by various items, passives, etc: See [[list of effects that modify corpse health]].


Corpse Health cannot be decreased until the unit's death animation is over.


Cats who innately have 100+ Corpse Health, can take infinite hits while downed, and revive from '''any''' healing.

=== Not leaving a body ===
Units who have 0 Corpse Health, do not leave a body.
* During their death animation, they are still considered as having a corpse however.
* This is most small units.

Non-Player Cat units will not leave a corpse, or play their death animation, if dealing damage equal to or higher than their current health + max health.
* As an example: 30 Damage to a 15 HP Tom Tom, or 16 damage to a 1 HP Tom Tom.
<!--30 damage against 15 hp tomtom, he explodes.-->
* Enemies with 0 max health are an exception to this. <!--, as otherwise it would always happen.-->

A unit with {{st|Infested}} does not leave a body.

If either {{i|Throbbing Gristle}} or {{i|Steven's Gristle}} are equipped by a unit, no unit leaves a body.
